This video has no design system yet. You can tell.
Purple gradients. Four fonts. Every corner a different curve. Everything bouncing.
It's what you get when an AI guesses.
So let's give it one, while you watch.
I'm OpenDesigner. I live inside the AI you already use, like Claude, ChatGPT, Codex or Cursor.
I ask a few plain questions, one at a time.
What are we making? A short film about this project.
Who is it for? People watching on a phone. So the type gets bigger, and there's less of it.
How should it feel? Premium, confident, warm. The gradients go. One typeface stays.
Any brand color? This orange. I darken it a little, so text on it stays readable.
Every answer becomes a token: color, type, spacing, corners, depth and motion.
Eight dials tune the feel. Here, they come from a taste poll of real, shipped apps.
Some rules never move: readable contrast, targets big enough to tap, visible focus, and calmer motion for those who need it.
Behind every default is research. Thirty-two design systems taken apart. Nearly two hundred questions. Over five hundred decision cards, each with its sources.
Then I write it all down: design tokens, CSS, Tailwind, Swift, Compose, Figma, and a DESIGN dot M D your agents can follow.
Seven more skills cover the rest. Learn from a site, extend a system, export it, illustrate it, review it, paint with it, and check it before you ship.
This is the same video, now on its own system.
OpenDesigner. Free and open source. Just ask your AI: create a design system for this project.
